html:
SMTO-CFG-0057 — Model temperature must be between 0 and 1

GUID: 35469b9e-f46b-4330-9d6a-d0c44b58badf
Slug: config-llm-request-temperature-must-be-between-0
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • SMTO only accepts a Model temperature — how varied the Model's answers are — from 0 to 1. If you were saving a user's settings, nothing was saved; if SMTO was starting, it stopped.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you saw this on the Users page, select Manage for that user, open Additional configuration, and set Model temperature from 0 to 1 (for example 0 or 0.2), or clear it. The box accepts numbers above 1, but SMTO only uses temperatures up to 1.
  2. Select Save user. The corrected value applies only after you save; an empty box uses the installation's value.
  3. If a user's workspace won't open with this error, an administrator should correct that user's Model temperature on the Users page, as in steps 1 and 2. Each workspace starts with its user's saved settings, so one bad saved value blocks it.
  4. If SMTO stopped while starting, find AOR_LLM_REQUEST_TEMPERATURE where SMTO is started, delete it (usual value 0) or set it from 0 to 1, then start SMTO again from there. At startup this temperature comes only from that setting.

What success looks like

  • The Users page shows Account updated, or the startup screen reaches Ready.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't change Model timeout or Maximum model output tokens to get past this error; they are separate settings.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Settings validation rejected llm_request_temperature (environment variable AOR_LLM_REQUEST_TEMPERATURE at startup, or a per-user configuration override) because it is outside the inclusive range 0 to 1.

What this means

  • llm_request_temperature lies outside the inclusive range zero through one. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • llm_request_temperature lies outside the inclusive range zero through one.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the request-temperature override separately from the provider's broader possible API range.

How to fix it

  • For a per-user override, set llm_request_temperature (Users > Manage > Additional configuration > Model temperature) to a value from 0 to 1 or remove it; WorkspaceManager.validate_changes rejects the save and user_settings rejects an already-saved bad value when that workspace starts. For startup, unset AOR_LLM_REQUEST_TEMPERATURE or set it from 0 to 1 (default 0.0) and restart. This is separate from llm.default_temperature (any value of 0 or more).
  • Set llm_request_temperature within zero through one.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A value in the application's supported 0–1 range validates.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
